claim.why_it_matters: The CURRENT-DATE character-position table is broken: its column headings sit outside the table as a mangled prose line ("Character Contents\ Positions"), the table ends at row 13-14, the two LEAP-SECOND sub-items are detached from the 13-14 row, and rows 15-16, 17, 18-19 and 20-21 fall out as unstructured indented paragraphs. The 15-16 row is further split mid-sentence ("in the range 00 through" / "99\. The value 00 ..."), so its upper bound 99 is detached into a separate paragraph that markdown renders as a stray numbered fragment. All text is present; the table structure that ties each position range to its contents is lost.

verdict.reasoning: Compared the 300-dpi render of PDF page 607 (printed 585) with page-607.md. Every word of the 15.16.2 table is present in the markdown in the printed order: the headings 'Character Positions' / 'Contents', rows 1-4 through 13-14 as table rows, the two LEAP-SECOND dashes directly after the 13-14 row, and rows 15-16, 17, 18-19 and 20-21 each starting with its position label followed by its full contents text. The claim itself concedes 'All text is present'. The '99\.' is an escaped period, so it renders as '99.' and not as a list item; the paragraph break between 'through' and '99' is a line-wrap artifact. Each position range still immediately precedes its contents and no value, range or condition changes. The defect is markdown table formatting and line wrapping only, which does not change meaning, so it is not a content discrepancy.
